rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Live-demo beats survive a text read.
rules_evaluated.evidence: No guess-before-reveal construction anywhere in the file, including the new Optional-challenges bullets: 'On a disposable branch, plant 20 plausible bugs. Run the current tests and count the catches. Then open a fresh review session, count again, and reveal your answer key' (line 79) is a student-run exercise instruction with the answer key deliberately withheld from the PAGE (the student holds it, not the reader) -- there is no authored guess/reveal pair on the slide itself for a reader to walk through out of order. This is a module file (metadata + LOs + ordered includes); any guess/predict beats belong to the included lectures/exercises, out of this file's scope.

Every chunk carries a self-standing claim: Big Idea's thesis (4), Prework's instruction + reading list (8-10), the five What-You'll-Learn LOs (14-18), Start here's framing + blockquote + two links, the worry-beside-the-artefact three-paragraph arc (32-36), Set-up-the-worktree's rationale + four includes + blockquote, the four Key Concepts lines, Back-to-the-map's four-paragraph closer, the new Optional-challenges' four concrete activity bullets (77-80) with its own framing line (75), Bring-to-Module-6's carry-forward instruction, the two pre-read annotations (93, 95), Next's two-sentence bridge (99). None is a bare wait-state or single context-dependent bullet.

'Big Idea', 'Prework', 'What You'll Learn', 'Key Concepts', 'Next' are architecture-mandated canonical section names (curriculum/module-shape.md), exempt from the plain-truth test by construction. 'Start here', 'Set up the worktree', 'Hold the worry beside the artefact', 'Back to the map, one last time', 'Bring to Module 6', 'Pre-reads before Module 6' all match their chunk's content on a plain read. 'Optional challenges' (line 73) is a literal match: the four bullets are all optional harder-mode activities, and line 75 ('Pick one when you want the test to bite harder') states exactly that -- no bait-and-switch between header and content.

Ran `sed -n '1,102p' learn-from-the-test.md | grep -niE "not [a-z]+\.? not |one of the most|most useful|about [0-9]+%|reached for|the bounded"` this session -- exit 1, zero matches body-wide, including the new Optional-challenges bullets. Line 63's edited quote ('cross personal -> team') is a two-word arrow phrase lifted verbatim from the source SVG (verified under rule 1), not a generated cadence tic.
